MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Round 553 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 550
   B. 540
   C. 560
   D. 500

2. What number is the Roman numeral X? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 10
   C. 3
   D. 1

3. In the number 6,092, the digit 6 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Thousands
   B. Tens
   C. Ones
   D. Hundreds

4. Which of these is a multiple of 9? (1 mark)
   A. 65
   B. 63
   C. 64
   D. 62

5. Which list shows all the factors of 42? (1 mark)
   A. 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21
   B. 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42
   C. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42
   D. 1, 2, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42

6. A trader saved Ksh 4,650 in the first term and Ksh 2,875 in the second term. How much did she save? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 7,525
   B. Ksh 6,425
   C. Ksh 7,515
   D. Ksh 7,625

7. Which word in a problem tells you to add? (1 mark)
   A. Altogether
   B. Fewer
   C. Remain
   D. Difference

8. Work out 5,127 + 2,864. (1 mark)
   A. 7,891
   B. 7,981
   C. 8,001
   D. 7,991

9. Work out 5,432 − 2,718. (1 mark)
   A. 2,724
   B. 3,326
   C. 2,714
   D. 2,614

10. Work out 45 × 18. (1 mark)
   A. 405
   B. 810
   C. 800
   D. 820

11. A jerrycan holds 20 litres. How many litres do 100 jerrycans hold? (1 mark)
   A. 2,100 litres
   B. 2,000 litres
   C. 1,990 litres
   D. 1,980 litres

12. 29 eggs are packed in trays that each hold 4 eggs. How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 9
   C. 7
   D. 8

13. Change 3 2/5 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 5/5
   B. 18/5
   C. 15/5
   D. 17/5

14. A rectangle is cut into 12 equal parts and 5 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 5/7
   B. 12/5
   C. 7/12
   D. 5/12

15. Change 11/4 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 3 2/4
   B. 3 3/4
   C. 2 3/4
   D. 2 4/4

16. Change 3 3/4 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 12/4
   B. 6/4
   C. 15/4
   D. 16/4

17. Change 19/4 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 5 3/4
   B. 4 3/4
   C. 4 4/4
   D. 3 4/4

18. Which is the smallest number: 1.2, 1.02, 1.25, 1.052? (1 mark)
   A. 1.2
   B. 1.02
   C. 1.052
   D. 1.25

19. What is the total value of the digit 4 in 13.42? (1 mark)
   A. 0.04
   B. 0.4
   C. 400
   D. 4

20. Write 3 1/10 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.31
   B. 3.01
   C. 3.1
   D. 31.0

21. If a = 4, what is the value of 3a? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 34
   C. 12
   D. 1

22. A square has sides of 6 cm. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 18 cm
   B. 36 cm
   C. 24 cm
   D. 12 cm

23. What is 8 m − 3 m 40 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 4 m 50 cm
   B. 4 m 70 cm
   C. 5 m 60 cm
   D. 4 m 60 cm

24. Change 250 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 3 m 50 cm
   B. 3 m
   C. 25 cm
   D. 2 m 50 cm

25. Rectangle P has 4 rows and 9 columns. Rectangle Q has 5 rows and 8 columns. Which has the bigger area? (1 mark)
   A. Rectangle Q
   B. It cannot be told
   C. Rectangle P
   D. They are equal

26. A rectangle has an area of 36 square units and 4 rows. How many columns does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 32
   B. 10
   C. 40
   D. 9

27. A tile is 10 cm long and 10 cm wide. It is covered with 1 cm squares. How many squares fit? (1 mark)
   A. 100
   B. 40
   C. 20
   D. 10

28. A rectangle is made of 9 rows with 4 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 13 square units
   B. 36 square units
   C. 26 square units
   D. 45 square units

29. A cuboid is 5 blocks long, 4 blocks wide and 4 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 20 blocks
   B. 85 blocks
   C. 80 blocks
   D. 13 blocks

30. What is 4 L − 1 3/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 2 3/4 L
   B. 2 1/2 L
   C. 2 L
   D. 2 1/4 L

31. What is 1/2 kg + 3 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 4 kg
   B. 3 1/2 kg
   C. 3 1/4 kg
   D. 3 3/4 kg

32. What is 2 1/4 kg + 1 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 3 3/4 kg
   B. 4 1/4 kg
   C. 4 kg
   D. 3 1/2 kg

33. What is 6 h − 2 h 15 min? (1 mark)
   A. 3 h 55 min
   B. 3 h 45 min
   C. 4 h 45 min
   D. 3 h 35 min

34. Change 28 days to weeks and days. (1 mark)
   A. 4 weeks
   B. 4 weeks 1 days
   C. 5 weeks
   D. 0 weeks 4 days

35. Change 135 minutes to hours and minutes. (1 mark)
   A. 2 h 15 min
   B. 3 h 15 min
   C. 2 h 45 min
   D. 1 h 45 min

36. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 9 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 6. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 9:30
   B. 6:45
   C. 10:30
   D. 9:06

37. A learner goes to bed at nine o'clock at night. How do we write this time? (1 mark)
   A. 9:00 noon
   B. 9:00 a.m.
   C. 9:30 p.m.
   D. 9:00 p.m.

38. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 6,500, Ksh 1,750 and Ksh 850. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 9,000
   B. Ksh 9,110
   C. Ksh 9,200
   D. Ksh 9,100

39. Kip faces South and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. West
   C. South
   D. North

40. In this grade we collect data of at most (1 mark)
   A. 100 items
   B. 5,000 items
   C. 1,000 items
   D. 10 items

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write 13.42 in expanded form and give the total value of the digit 4. (3 marks)

42. A farmer packs 84 mangoes equally into 4 baskets. How many mangoes are in each basket? Then he picks 3 more mangoes. Can he share all 87 mangoes equally among the 4 baskets? Explain. (5 marks)

43. Write 4 3/8 as an improper fraction. (3 marks)

44. List all the factors of 36. (3 marks)

45. A shop sells 3 packets of milk of 1/2 L each and 2 packets of 1 L each. How many litres of milk is that altogether? (3 marks)

46. A dial scale has big marks for each kilogram and three small marks between them. What mass does the first small mark after 3 kg show? Explain. (3 marks)

47. A learner says 3 weeks is 20 days. Explain her mistake and give the correct number of days. (3 marks)

48. Explain why we should change lengths to centimetres before adding 3 m 45 cm and 2 m 80 cm. (3 marks)

49. A buyer picks biscuits at Ksh 50, juice at Ksh 80 and a book at Ksh 120. He pays with a Ksh 500 note. Find the total cost and his change. (4 marks)

50. A trader has 25 kg of rice. She sells 7 1/2 kg to one customer and 6 3/4 kg to another. How much rice does she have left? (5 marks)

51. A bus carried 5,684 passengers on Saturday and 3,749 on Sunday. Find the total number of passengers and check your answer by adding in the opposite order. (4 marks)

52. A group of five tallies and 3 more tally marks show which number? Explain how you count. (2 marks)

53. Name the plane figure of each object: a plate, a floor tile, a door. (3 marks)

54. A square garden has sides of 15 m. Find the perimeter of the garden. (2 marks)

55. A shop earned Ksh 4,750 on Monday and Ksh 3,895 on Tuesday. How much did it earn on the two days? (3 marks)

56. Change 250 cm to metres and centimetres, and then to metres using a decimal. (3 marks)

57. Ten pupils chose their favourite drink: 4 chose juice, 3 chose milk, 2 chose water and 1 chose tea. Write two facts that you can read from this data. (2 marks)

58. A film begins at 4:20 p.m. and runs for 1 hour 40 minutes. Find the time at which it ends. (2 marks)

59. Change 11/4 to a mixed fraction and then change your answer back to an improper fraction to check it. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 550
   Look at the ones digit 3. It is less than 5, so keep the tens digit. 553 rounds to 550.

2. B — 10
   X stands for 10.

3. A — Thousands
   Counting from the right the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands. The digit 6 is in the thousands place.

4. B — 63
   63 = 9 × 7, so 63 is a multiple of 9.

5. B — 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42
   Pair up numbers that multiply to 42. The factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42.

6. A — Ksh 7,525
   Add 4,650 + 2,875 = 7,525 Ksh.

7. A — Altogether
   Altogether means put the amounts together, so we add.

8. D — 7,991
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 5,127 + 2,864 = 7,991.

9. C — 2,714
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 5,432 − 2,718 = 2,714. Check: 2,714 + 2,718 = 5,432.

10. B — 810
   45 × 8 = 360 and 45 × 10 = 450. 360 + 450 = 810.

11. B — 2,000 litres
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 2,000 litres.

12. D — 8
   29 ÷ 4 = 7 remainder 1. The 1 left-over eggs need one more tray, so 8 trays are needed.

13. D — 17/5
   3 × 5 = 15 and 15 + 2 = 17. The denominator stays 5, so the answer is 17/5.

14. D — 5/12
   The whole has 12 equal parts and 5 are shaded, so 5/12 is shaded.

15. C — 2 3/4
   11 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 3. The whole number is 2 and the fraction is 3/4, so 11/4 = 2 3/4.

16. C — 15/4
   3 × 4 = 12 and 12 + 3 = 15. The denominator stays 4, so the answer is 15/4.

17. B — 4 3/4
   19 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 3. The whole number is 4 and the fraction is 3/4, so 19/4 = 4 3/4.

18. B — 1.02
   Give every number the same number of decimal places and compare from the left. The smallest number is 1.02.

19. B — 0.4
   The digit 4 is in the tenths place, so its total value is 0.4.

20. C — 3.1
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 3 1/10 = 3.1.

21. C — 12
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 12.

22. C — 24 cm
   A square has four equal sides. 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24.

23. D — 4 m 60 cm
   800 − 340 = 460 cm = 4 m 60 cm.

24. D — 2 m 50 cm
   250 ÷ 100 = 2 remainder 50. So 250 cm = 2 m 50 cm.

25. A — Rectangle Q
   P = 4 × 9 = 36 and Q = 5 × 8 = 40. Rectangle Q has the bigger area.

26. D — 9
   Rows × columns = 36, so columns = 36 ÷ 4 = 9.

27. A — 100
   10 rows × 10 columns = 100 squares.

28. B — 36 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 9 × 4 = 36 square units.

29. C — 80 blocks
   One layer has 5 × 4 = 20 blocks. There are 4 layers, so the volume is 20 × 4 = 80 blocks.

30. D — 2 1/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 4 L − 1 3/4 L = 2 1/4 L.

31. B — 3 1/2 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 1/2 kg + 3 kg = 3 1/2 kg.

32. A — 3 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 2 1/4 kg + 1 1/2 kg = 3 3/4 kg.

33. B — 3 h 45 min
   Change 1 hour to 60 minutes when the minutes are not enough. The answer is 3 h 45 min.

34. A — 4 weeks
   28 ÷ 7 = 4 remainder 0, so 28 days = 4 weeks.

35. A — 2 h 15 min
   135 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 15, so 135 minutes = 2 h 15 min.

36. A — 9:30
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 6 shows 6 × 5 = 30 minutes, so the time is 9:30.

37. D — 9:00 p.m.
   Times from midnight to noon use a.m. and times from noon to midnight use p.m. The correct answer is 9:00 p.m..

38. D — Ksh 9,100
   Add the three costs: 6,500 + 1,750 + 850 = 9,100.

39. B — West
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. South followed by a quarter turn clockwise gives West.

40. D — 10 items
   To keep counting easy and accurate we collect at most 10 items.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10 + 3 + 0.4 + 0.02. The total value of 4 is 0.4 (4 tenths).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 10 + 3, 1 mark for 0.4 + 0.02, 1 mark for the total value of 4.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: 21 mangoes in each basket. 87 ÷ 4 = 21 remainder 3, so he cannot share all 87 equally; 3 will be left over.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 21, 2 marks for 87 ÷ 4 = 21 R 3 with working, 1 mark for answering no, 1 mark for the explanation.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 35/8
   Working / marking points: 4 × 8 = 32 (1 mark); 32 + 3 = 35 (1 mark); denominator stays 8 (1 mark).

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36
   Working / marking points: Pairs: 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 4 × 9, 6 × 6. 3 marks for all nine factors, 2 marks for seven or eight, 1 mark for at least five.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 L
   Working / marking points: 3 × 1/2 = 1 1/2 L (1 mark); 2 × 1 = 2 L (1 mark); total 3 1/2 L (1 mark).

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/4 kg. The three small marks divide each kilogram into four equal parts of 1/4 kg.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 3 1/4 kg, 1 mark for four equal parts, 1 mark for 1/4 kg each.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 week has 7 days, so 3 weeks is 3 × 7 = 21 days.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7 days in a week, 1 mark for multiplying by 3, 1 mark for 21 days.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: When both lengths are in centimetres we can add them like ordinary numbers: 345 + 280 = 625 cm. This avoids mistakes with regrouping 100 cm into 1 m.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using one unit, 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for reference to regrouping.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Total Ksh 250; change Ksh 250
   Working / marking points: 50 + 80 + 120 = 250 (2 marks); 500 − 250 = 250 (2 marks).

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: 10 3/4 kg
   Working / marking points: Total sold: 7 1/2 + 6 3/4 = 7 2/4 + 6 3/4 = 13 5/4 = 14 1/4 kg (3 marks). 25 − 14 1/4 = 10 3/4 kg (2 marks).

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: 9,433 passengers. Check: 3,749 + 5,684 = 9,433.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for correct working with regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with unit, 1 mark for the check.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: 8. Count the group of five as 5, then add 3 more: 5 + 3 = 8.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 8 and 1 mark for the explanation.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plate: circle. Floor tile: square. Door: rectangle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct shape.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: 60 m
   Working / marking points: 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 = 60 m. 1 mark for method and 1 mark for answer with unit.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 8,645
   Working / marking points: 4,750 + 3,895. Ones 5; tens 5 + 9 = 14 write 4 carry 1; hundreds 7 + 8 + 1 = 16 write 6 carry 1; thousands 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. 1 mark for setting up, 1 for regrouping, 1 for the answer with units.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 m 50 cm and 2.5 m
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dividing by 100, 1 mark for 2 m 50 cm, 1 mark for 2.5 m.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: juice is the most popular with 4 pupils; only 1 pupil chose tea; 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 pupils were asked.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fact based on the numbers.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: 6:00 p.m.
   Working / marking points: 4:20 + 1 h = 5:20 p.m. (1 mark); + 40 min = 6:00 p.m. (1 mark).

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: 11/4 = 2 3/4. Check: 2 × 4 = 8 and 8 + 3 = 11, so 11/4.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 2 3/4 with working, 2 marks for the correct check.
